target_concept: Contrast deterministic point encoding of standard autoencoders with probabilistic encoding of VAEs

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly describes an advantage of variational autoencoders (VAEs) compared to standard deterministic autoencoders?
options: They encode each input as a single deterministic latent vector.
They model the latent representation as a distribution (mean and variance) allowing sampling and smoother latent space.
They require less computational resources than standard autoencoders.
They guarantee perfect reconstruction of the input image.
mcq.correctAnswer: They model the latent representation as a distribution (mean and variance) allowing sampling and smoother latent space.
mcq.explanation: VAEs encode inputs probabilistically by learning a mean and variance for each latent dimension, which captures the data distribution and enables sampling and better generalization. Standard autoencoders produce a single fixed latent point, lacking these benefits.
